name: Senua

attributes.attribute: statue found in a hoard of 26 objects

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Senua is a British goddess of water and healing. Her broken silver statue was found in 2002. A metal detector led an amateur guess to it in Hertfordshire. The statue was part of a hoard of 26 precious objects hidden in the earth during the late third century, perhaps at a time of danger. Years of burial wore down the Romanized metal. X-rays at the British Museum showed the figure in the garb of Minerva and read out her name. Senua was dear to a small spring and to healing. She returned from the earth after 1,600 years. Her return is a sign that much of Celtic religion still lies out of reach of the modern eye.
